claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start by asking: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son **Alex**.

Before I can assess eligibility, I need to understand your specific circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 17 years old.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex is 17 and not in full-time education or training, I need to clarify an important point:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you at home.

Now I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have a right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Before I can make a final decision, I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I'm assessing your situation correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the eligibility rules, and I've identified an important issue with Alex's eligibility.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify if your child is under 16. However, if your child is **16 or over**, you'll normally still qualify **only if** they stay in **approved education or training**.

Since Alex is 17 and is **not** in full-time education or training, he would not normally qualify for Child Benefit.

However, there is one potential exception: you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old **leaves education or training and registers** with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education/training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to make my assessment.

Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can provide you with my decision:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Decision: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Reason:** Alex is 17 years old and is not in approved full-time education or training. According to Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally only claim for a child aged 16 or over if they remain in approved education or training. 

While there is an exception that allows for a 20-week continuation period if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, Alex has not done so, which means he does not qualify.

If Alex does register with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services in the future, you may be able to claim the 20-week continuation period. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office if this situation changes.
